### Monetized Non-Core Assets, Added Core Acreage While Advancing Higher-Return Development Program and Reducing Debt


THE WOODLANDS, Texas, Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ring Energy, Inc. (NYSE American: REI) (“Ring” or the “Company”) today reported operational and financial results for the third quarter of 2026 and provided an update on its guidance, development program, portfolio optimization initiatives and balance sheet.


During the third quarter, Ring continued to execute its strategy of improving its capital efficiency and the quality of its asset portfolio while strengthening its balance sheet. The Company completed approximately $30.5 million of non-core asset sales, acquired approximately $18.8 million of leasehold interests in the Central Basin Platform (“CBP”) and reduced borrowings under its revolving credit facility by $10.0 million. The acquired leasehold is positioned within Ring's existing CBP operating footprint, supporting the Company's strategy of expanding higher-return development inventory while increasing financial flexibility. Subsequent to the quarter, on October 30th, Ring closed another divestiture of non-core assets in Gaines and Andrews Counties for ~ $13.4 million.


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights**


*(Comparisons are to the second quarter of 2026 unless otherwise noted.)*


Delivered Higher Adjusted Earnings Despite Lower Realized Oil Prices


- Generated $102.3 million of revenue, down ~ 2% from $104.7 million, primarily reflecting lower realized oil prices;
- Realized oil price of $83.72 per barrel, down ~ 12%;
- Reported net loss of $16.6 million, or $0.06 per diluted share, including a $41.0 million unrealized loss on commodity derivative contracts;
- Adjusted Net Income1 of $27.3 million, or $0.10 per diluted share, up ~ 14% from $24.0 million;
- Adjusted EBITDA1 of $57.1 million, up ~ 5% from $54.5 million despite lower realized oil prices; and
- Net cash provided by operating activities of $63.1 million.


High-Graded Portfolio and Strengthened Balance Sheet


- Completed non-core asset divestitures of ~ 130 barrels of oil equivalent per day ("Boe/d") (63% oil) and ~ 9.8k net acres for ~ $30.5 million;
- Acquired ~ 16.5k net acres for $18.8 million of leasehold interests in the CBP, expanding Ring's core development footprint by over 25% in Crane and Ector Counties; and
- Reduced borrowings under the Company’s revolving credit facility by $10.0 million to $350.0 million at September 30, 2026, while improving LQA leverage ratio to 1.5x from 1.7x.


Advanced Higher-Return Development Program


- Sales volumes of ~ 20,635 Boe/d, including ~ 12,818 barrels of oil per day ("Bo/d"), up approximately 3% and 1%, respectively;
- Brought online first 2-mile horizontal wells and drilled nine YTD;
- Reduced drilling and completion costs2 to ~ $475 per foot YTD; and
- Invested ~ $64.0 million, reflecting the deliberate acceleration of drilling and infrastructure investments to transition to a more capital-efficient program.


Continued Cost Discipline


- Reported lease operating expense ("LOE") of $10.20 per Boe, below the mid-point of guidance;
- Interest expense of $7.7 million, down ~ 23% year-over-year, reflecting lower debt balances; and
- Reduced all-in-cash costs by 3% to $21.03 per Boe.


**Subsequent Events and Updating Guidance**


- On October 30th, closed a divestiture of non-core assets in Gaines and Andrews Counties for ~ $13.4 million representing ~470 Boe/d (77% oil) of production;
- Q4 2026 oil production guidance range of 12,900 to 13,500 Bopd and total sales range of 20,400 to 21,200 Boepd;
- Q4 2026 LOE per Boe guidance range of $9.80 to $10.30; and
- Updating 2027 guidance pro forma for divestitures.


**Management Commentary**


Paul D. McKinney, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, commented:


“This was an exciting and highly productive quarter for Ring. We delivered strong operational results, advanced our longer-lateral development program and took decisive steps to improve the depth and quality of our portfolio. In a single quarter, we monetized approximately $30.5 million of non-core assets, added strategic acreage in the heart of our Central Basin Platform position and reduced debt by $10.0 million.


With strong commodity prices, encouraging well performance and the cash surplus from asset dispositions, we deliberately chose to outspend adjusted free cash flow this quarter to accelerate our program. Having said that, we have not lost our focus on capital discipline – we intend to be cash flow positive during the fourth quarter and for the full year. We are proud of what our team accomplished so far this year and remain focused on debt reduction and improving our leverage ratio metrics.


Operationally, we grew production 3% from the second quarter and kept lease operating expense below the mid-point of our guidance range while drilling eight horizontal wells and completing seven, including our first five, 2-mile co-developed laterals in Crane County. These results reinforce our confidence in the development program and demonstrate the execution capability of our team.


The acreage we acquired is particularly compelling because it expands our inventory within an area we know well, where we already operate and where we see attractive opportunities to generate strong returns. By selling assets that were not expected to compete for near-term capital, we effectively recycled capital from lower-priority assets into higher-quality inventory while also strengthening the balance sheet. We believe this is a compelling example of how disciplined capital allocation can strengthen Ring and create stockholder value. We intend for this to be an integral part of our strategy going forward.


We entered 2026 focused on moving Ring into its next phase with greater capital efficiency, and the progress we made this quarter represents an important step forward. We have a stronger portfolio with a deeper inventory of low break-even development opportunities and greater financial flexibility. We are energized by the momentum across the business and believe Ring is increasingly well positioned to deliver durable and competitive, per-share value for our stockholders.”

**Balance Sheet and Liquidity**


Total liquidity (defined as cash and cash equivalents plus borrowing base availability under the Company’s credit facility) at September 30, 2026 was approximately $236.4 million, consisting of $235.0 million of availability under our revolving credit facility, which included a reduction of $35 thousand for letters of credit, and approximately $1.5 million in cash and cash equivalents. On September 30, 2026, the Company had $350 million in borrowings outstanding on its credit facility that has a current borrowing base of $585 million. This reflects a reduction of $10 million from the balance of $360 million at June 30, 2026. The Company intends to continue debt reduction, dependent on market conditions, the timing and level of capital spending, and other considerations.


**Drilling and Completion Activity**


In 3Q 2026, the Company drilled a total of eight and completed a total of seven horizontal producing wells. Additionally, the Company completed the SWD well that was in the process of being drilled at the end of the second quarter. In the Central Basin Platform in Andrews County, the Company drilled and completed two 1.5-mile horizontal wells, both with a working interest of approximately 99%. In the Central Basin Platform in Crane County, the Company drilled six and completed five 2-mile horizontal wells, each with a working interest of 100%.

**Remaining Quarter of** **2026** **and Full-Year 2027 Sales Volumes, Capital Investment and Operating Expense Guidance**


Since providing its original 2026 development outlook, Ring has continued to refine its development plan towards horizontal drilling and allocate capital toward its highest-return opportunities. This evolution reflects encouraging early well results, improved operational execution and the attractive economics associated with extended-reach laterals. Ring believes the increased concentration of longer lateral opportunities has the potential to enhance capital efficiency, improve project economics and support the Company's strategy of generating higher returns while responsibly growing production.

**Non-GAAP Financial Information**


Certain financial information included in this release are not measures of financial performance recognized by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP financial measures are “Adjusted Net Income,” “Adjusted EBITDA,” “Adjusted Free Cash Flow” or “AFCF,” “Adjusted Cash Flow from Operations” or “ACFFO,” “G&A Excluding Share-Based Compensation,” “G&A Excluding Share-Based Compensation and Transaction Costs,” “Leverage Ratio,” “Consolidated Total Debt to LQA Consolidated EBITDAX,” “All-In Cash Operating Costs,” and “Cash Operating Margin.” Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures in its analysis of performance. These disclosures may not be viewed as a substitute for results determined in accordance with GAAP and are not necessarily comparable to non-GAAP performance measures which may be reported by other companies.


**Reconciliation of** **Net income (loss)** **to** **Adjusted Net Income**


“Adjusted Net Income” is calculated as net income (loss) minus the estimated after-tax impact of share-based compensation, ceiling test impairment, unrealized gains and losses on changes in the fair value of derivatives, and transaction costs for acquisitions and divestitures (“A&D”). Adjusted Net Income is presented because the timing and amount of these items cannot be reasonably estimated and affect the comparability of operating results from period to period, and current period to prior periods. The Company believes that the presentation of Adjusted Net Income provides useful information to investors as it is one of the metrics management uses to assess the Company’s ongoing operating and financial performance, and also is a useful metric for investors to compare the Company’s results with its peers.

**Reconciliations of Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities to Adjusted Free Cash Flow and Adjusted EBITDA to Adjusted Free Cash Flow**


The Company defines “Adjusted Free Cash Flow” or “AFCF” as Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities (as reflected on the Company’s Condensed Statements of Cash Flows) less changes in operating assets and liabilities, and plus transaction costs for acquisitions and divestitures (“A&D”), current income tax expense (benefit), proceeds from divestitures of oil and natural gas properties, loss (gain) on disposal of assets, and less capital expenditures, credit loss expense, and other income. Management believes that Adjusted Free Cash Flow is an important financial performance measure for use in evaluating the performance and efficiency of the Company’s current operating activities after the impact of capital expenditures and net interest expense (including interest income and expense, excluding amortization of deferred financing costs) and without being impacted by items such as changes associated with working capital, which can vary substantially from one period to another. Other companies may use different definitions of Adjusted Free Cash Flow.

**Calculation of Leverage Ratio**


“Leverage” or the “Leverage Ratio” is calculated pursuant to the Company’s existing senior revolving credit facility and means as of any date, the ratio of (i) Consolidated Total Debt as of such date to (ii) Consolidated EBITDAX for the four consecutive fiscal quarters ending on or immediately prior to such date for which financial statements are required to have been delivered under the credit facility.


The Company defines “Consolidated Total Debt” in accordance with its existing senior revolving credit facility and means, as of any date, all Indebtedness of the Company on a consolidated basis as of such date, but excluding hedging obligations.


The Company defines “Indebtedness” in accordance with its existing senior revolving credit facility and generally means (i) all obligations of the Company for borrowed money, (ii) all obligations of the Company evidenced by notes or other similar instruments, (iii) all obligations of the Company in respect of the deferred purchase price of property or services, (iv) all obligations of the Company under any conditional sale relating to property acquired the Company, (v) all capital lease obligations of the Company, (vi) all obligations, contingent or otherwise, of the Company in respect of letters of credit or similar extensions of credit, (vii) all guarantees of the Company of the type of Indebtedness described in clauses (i) through (vi) above, (viii) all Indebtedness of a third party secured by any lien on property owned by the Company, whether or not such Indebtedness has been assumed by the Company, (ix) all off-balance sheet liabilities, (x) all hedging obligations and (xi) the undischarged balance of any production payment created by the Company or for the creation of which the Company directly or indirectly received payment.


The Company defines “Consolidated EBITDAX” in accordance with its existing senior revolving credit facility and means for any period an amount equal to the sum of (i) consolidated net income (loss) for such period plus (ii) to the extent deducted in determining consolidated net income (loss) for such period, and without duplication, (A) consolidated interest expense, (B) income tax expense (benefit) determined on a consolidated basis, (C) depreciation, depletion and amortization determined on a consolidated basis, (D) exploration expenses determined on a consolidated basis, and (E) all other non-cash charges reasonably acceptable to the administrative agent, in each case for such period minus (iii) all noncash income added to consolidated net income (loss) for such period; provided that, for purposes of calculating compliance with the financial covenants under the credit facility, to the extent that during such period the Company has consummated an acquisition permitted by the credit facility or any sale, transfer or other disposition of any property or assets permitted by the credit facility, Consolidated EBITDAX will be calculated on a pro forma basis with respect to the property or assets acquired or disposed of.

The Company defines Consolidated Total Debt to LQA Consolidated EBITDAX as Consolidated Total Debt divided by LQA (“Last Quarter Annualized”) Consolidated EBITDAX. Consolidated Total Debt and Consolidated EBITDAX are defined pursuant to the Company’s existing senior revolving credit facility. The Company believes this metric is more reflective of its current leverage ratio profile by annualizing Consolidated EBITDAX for the most recent period. Consolidated Total Debt to LQA Consolidated EBITDAX and Consolidated EBTIDAX are non-GAAP financial measures and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies and should not be considered as a substitute for measured prepared in accordance with GAAP. Therefore, the Company believes it is important to view this ratio and Consolidated EBITDAX as supplemental to its entire financial statements.
